claim: test_changeset_builder.md's "Cross-component scenario: spec_node_kind per declared type comes from the profile" (added by the declarative-profile spec change) asserts: "Under the extended profile, the endpoint create's op carries the declared spec_node_kind (\"endpoint\") unchanged, composed through the same canonical field order with no new op shape" — i.e. Build() succeeds end to end for a create whose NodeType is a profile-declared type outside today's four-entry vocabulary (component, data_flow, test_section, proposal_epic).
authoritative_source: arch_topological_sorter.md, "Interface": "Two kinds of batch yield an error and no ordering at all: one holding a cycle, and one holding a create whose spec node kind belongs to no tier." arch_resolver.md, "Every ref names a node that can own a bead": "the sorter refuses to tier a create whose kind it does not recognise." Neither file was touched by the declarative-profile commit (4d37093) that added the endpoint scenario, and TopologicalSorter's implemented tier table (plan/sorter.go, var tierOf) is a fixed 4-entry map with no profile awareness — unlike ActionClassifier's planRelevant gate, which already reads graph.profileOrDefault().PlanRelevant.
evidence: Probed Build() directly with an action carrying NodeType: "endpoint" (what ActionClassifier would emit under a profile declaring endpoint plan-relevant, per test_classification.md's own already-passing scenario for that gate). Build() returned: "plan: build: plan: sort: spec node e1 has kind \"endpoint\", which belongs to no tier" — no changeset, no op, per TopologicalSorter's documented and implemented refusal. ChangesetBuilder's own contract (arch_changeset_builder.md) is internally consistent — it copies Action.NodeType into spec_node_kind verbatim and validates nothing against the vocabulary table — but the composition as a whole cannot produce the changeset the new scenario asserts, because a sibling component this bead does not own (TopologicalSorter) refuses the batch before ChangesetBuilder ever assembles the op. Fixing this requires either a profile-driven tier assignment in TopologicalSorter (a behavior change to a component with its own owning bead and its own arch/test leaves) or narrowing the scenario's premise, neither of which this bead's leaves (arch_changeset_builder.md, test_changeset_builder.md, flow_plan.md, module.json) authorize.
proposed_fix: Either (a) give the resolved profile an explicit tier declaration per plan-relevant type (new types default to the features/data_flow tier unless stated otherwise), teach TopologicalSorter to consult it instead of the hardcoded tierOf map, and revise arch_topological_sorter.md/arch_resolver.md's "refuses unknown kind" language to describe refusing only a kind absent from the resolved profile's tier declarations; or (b) narrow test_changeset_builder.md's scenario to state that a profile-declared plan-relevant type must map onto one of today's three tiers (an authoring constraint on profile.json), and flip the extended-profile assertion to expect Build() to error naming the ungated kind, matching TopologicalSorter's current, unmodified contract.
